speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: Prime Minister Lee Hsien Loong and Indonesian President Joko Widodo held their Leaders' Retreat on 25 January 2022 in Bintan, Indonesia.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: Following the Leaders' Retreat, several Members have filed Parliamentary Questions, regarding the nature of the agreements and their impact on Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: Minister Iswaran and I will address Questions for Oral Answer filed by several Members, namely, Mr Gan Thiam Poh, Ms Poh Li San, Mr Saktiandi Supaat, Mr Melvin Yong, Mr Lim Biow Chuan, Mr Pritam Singh and a Question for Written Answer filed by Miss Cheryl Chan from today's Order Paper, as well as the Question for Oral Answer filed by Mr Gerald Giam1 for a future Sitting.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: I will cover the principles upon which the Expanded Framework was negotiated, the main elements of the agreements, their implications for our bilateral relations and the implementation of the agreements.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: Minister Iswaran will elaborate with further details on the FIR Agreement.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: The FIR, extradition and military training issues have been on our bilateral agenda for several decades.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: I had been personally involved in handling some of these issues at various points in time during my previous career in the SAF and, subsequently, as a Cabinet Minister.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: The 1995 military training agreement was implemented but lapsed after a few years.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: In 2007, we made another attempt and concluded agreements on the DCA and ET, and agreed to implement them simultaneously.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: However, the agreements were not ratified by Indonesia.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: In 2019, President Jokowi was elected to a second term.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: Prime Minister Lee and President Jokowi enjoy a good relationship, and our two countries and governments have strong ties.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: Both leaders were of the view that the conditions were right to discuss and resolve the outstanding issues decisively, in an open, constructive and mutually beneficial manner.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: Prime Minister Lee and President Jokowi tasked me and Coordinating Minister Luhut, whom I know well, to put maximum effort into this.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: The Framework laid out a set of considerations and principles, and acknowledged that the core interests and rights of both countries must be recognised and respected.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: In the course of the negotiations, in April 2021, at Indonesia's request, we expanded this Framework to include the ET.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: Our two countries have worked together on this issue before.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: It was in our interests to reach an agreement on the extradition of fugitives that would strengthen our bilateral cooperation in tackling criminal matters.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: The inclusion of the ET would help conclude a set of agreements on these three outstanding issues that would be acceptable to both sides.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: The set of agreements under the Expanded Framework for Discussions was carefully negotiated to achieve a good balance of benefits for both sides which are durable and for the long haul.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: It is underpinned by full respect for the sovereignty of both countries.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: It is in accordance with international law, in particular, the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS), and protects our mutual interests.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: At the Leaders' Retreat, both governments also exchanged letters undertaking to bring the three agreements that we have reached – on the FIR, Extradition and Defence Cooperation – into force simultaneously.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: FIR arrangements are established under ICAO for the purpose of managing civil aircraft in order to ensure the safety and efficiency of air traffic and to advance international civil aviation.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: Members would be aware that Indonesia had expressed its desire to realign the FIR boundaries in accordance with its expanded territorial waters which include archipelagic waters newly provided for under UNCLOS in 1982.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: Singapore's interest was the present and future needs of Changi Airport, which Indonesia accepted.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: The FIR Agreement that we concluded under our Expanded Framework addressed these key considerations.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: Singapore and Indonesia agreed to realign the boundary between the Singapore and Jakarta FIRs, largely taking into account Indonesia's archipelagic and territorial baselines, which were deposited with the UN in 2009.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: Indonesia will also delegate to Singapore the provision of air navigation services in portions of the airspace within the realigned Jakarta FIR, to ensure that present and future traffic to Changi Airport and nearby Indonesian airports continue to be managed safely and efficiently.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: When all the agreements under the Expanded Framework have been ratified through our respective domestic processes, Singapore and Indonesia will jointly seek ICAO's approval for these new FIR arrangements.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: We believe that the FIR arrangements will benefit the aviation sectors of both countries and airspace users in the region.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: Minister Iswaran will elaborate further on the specifics of the agreement in his Ministerial Statement.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: On military training, the Singapore and Indonesian governments agreed to ratify and bring into force the DCA and the Implementing Arrangement between the SAF and the Indonesian Armed Forces for the Military Training Area in Indonesia – both agreements as signed in 2007.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: Our two defence establishments have enjoyed decades of close friendship.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: As common security challenges become more complex, we need to work together closely all the more.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: The DCA will strengthen cooperation between our armed forces and advance our bilateral defence relations.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: It will facilitate the discussion and oversight of new areas of defence cooperation between our two defence establishments.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: The SAF has been conducting its training in the designated South China Sea Danger Area (SCSDA) since the 1960s, when the area was international waters.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: Subsequently, parts of the SCSDA became Indonesian archipelagic and territorial waters and airspace under UNCLOS.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: However, the SAF's training activities in such areas continue, as a right provided for under Article 51 of UNCLOS.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: The third agreement we signed was the Extradition Treaty or ET.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: Under the ET, Singapore and Indonesia will grant extradition for a comprehensive list of extraditable offences covered by the treaty, in accordance with the laws of both countries and subject to the requisite safeguards and provisions in the ET.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: The ET is substantively similar to the treaty that we had signed in 2007.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: We believe that the extension will provide more flexibility in the scope of cooperation for both countries.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: The benefits of the ET to both countries are clear.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: It will strengthen cooperation between our law enforcement agencies in combatting crime.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: Our hope is that the ET will also be helpful to Indonesia's own efforts to prevent suspected criminals from fleeing overseas and for them to be apprehended in Indonesia.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: Even without an ET, we already work closely with Indonesia to tackle these criminal matters.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: The ET will complement our existing cooperation with Indonesia through the ASEAN Treaty on Mutual Legal Assistance in Criminal Matters (ASEAN MLAT) and other multilateral treaties that we are party to.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: It also adds to Singapore's extradition arrangements with many jurisdictions across the globe.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: More fundamentally, the ET reflects both countries' commitment to work with international partners to combat crime and uphold the rule of law.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: This will help to enhance Singapore's role as a responsible and effective member of the international community, with a positive impact on our already good standing and reputation as a global financial hub.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: We have had negotiations on these issues since the 1990s.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: Singapore has always approached these discussions with our close neighbour Indonesia with sincerity and in the spirit of cooperation.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: We strive to reach a balance of benefits, taking into account each other's rights and interests.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: This was our approach in 1995 and in 2007, when we had previously reached agreement on these issues, though the agreements had subsequently either lapsed or could not be implemented for reasons beyond our control.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: We have maintained this same spirit and approach through the years.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: The negotiations to arrive at this set of agreements under the Expanded Framework involved many rounds of negotiations since 2019, made even more challenging by the fact that most of the negotiations were carried out during the COVID-19 period.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: Our negotiators spent many weeks in quarantine as a result of that and we have many Zoom meetings.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: We were able to reach agreement between Prime Minister Lee and President Jokowi because both had a strong desire to resolve these issues decisively and amicably, based on the Framework they endorsed.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: This set of agreements represents a win-win outcome.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: They are balanced, mutually beneficial and durable agreements for the long haul.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: They will provide a strong foundation to further strengthen our bilateral relations.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: Both sides are currently going through their respective domestic processes to ratify these agreements.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: Both Prime Minister Lee and President Jokowi have expressed the desire to ratify and bring these agreements into force simultaneously, soon.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: Mr Saktiandi Supaat and Mr Pritam Singh asked what will happen at the end of the 25-year duration of the FIR Agreement.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: I should first say that the duration of the FIR Agreement, 25 years, will provide a durable and firm basis for cooperation in this important area for a generation or more.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: Singapore and Indonesia recognise that we will always be neighbours and that we should continue to work together as partners.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: This agreement and the principles underlying it provide a good basis for future cooperation where each side brings something to the table and we work together to create a larger outcome, where the whole is bigger than the sum of all its parts.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: We certainly hope and have confidence that, after 25 years, this same spirit will prevail.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: We had a capable and cohesive negotiating team, who identified our interests clearly and pushed for them energetically and diplomatically.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: We had capable and committed negotiating partners, too, on the Indonesian side, who also worked very hard to push for their interests.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: But both sides also knew that we had a shared interest in closer bilateral cooperation and the benefits that that would bring.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: As a result, we were able to reach a good set of agreements that are win-win.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: The most important factor to ensure that Singapore always has a good hand to bring to the table in any negotiations, is to have a strong, clear thinking, trustworthy and capable Government which is supported by a united people.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: It gives me particular satisfaction to have played some part in this latest chapter in our long-standing cooperation.
